parts:
On Monday, October 8, 2012 11:21:43 AM UTC-4, Shige wrote:

I want to run the missing data example on the Stan reference manual (p. 32), where can the data?

That code was intended to be abstract, so there are no actual data. The attached R file generates some data and then uses stan() in the rstan package to execute "the" code in section 7.1 of the Stan manual. I put "the" in quotes because my code uses the vectorized version of the normal distribution, rather than looping over the values of y_obs and y_miss.

See also this thread:

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/mEGf1RFBlcU/discussion

Ben

Hi Ben,

Suppose, among the 101 generated y_miss values, the first (y_miss_1) and the last (y_miss_101) are of the most importance and I want to extract their posterior distributions and compute the posterior for their first difference (y_miss_101 - y_miss_1), can this be done? I am reading the "extract" method but it is not clear how to do what I have in mind here.

Thanks.

best,
Shige

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: How to run examples in the Stan reference manual?
parts:
On Monday, October 8, 2012 8:51:48 PM UTC-4, Shige wrote:
Suppose, among the 101 generated y_miss values, the first (y_miss_1) and the last (y_miss_101) are of the most importance and I want to extract their posterior distributions and compute the posterior for their first difference (y_miss_101 - y_miss_1), can this be done? I am reading the "extract" method but it is not clear how to do what I have in mind here.

In R, you can do

y_diff <- -apply(extract(results, c("y_miss[1]", "y_miss[101]")), 1:2, diff)

but it is probably better to make a generated quantity in your .stan file

generated quantities {
  real y_diff;
  y_diff <- y_miss[101] - y_miss[1];
}

Ben

Thanks.

best,
Shige
